Built for the gap.

A closer look at the mechanics described in the FloatSheets product overview and backend specification.

IN THIS NOTELeverage follows liquidity.No normal fills during a halt.Corporate actions need explicit transitions.A defined loss waterfall.Risk that remains.Explore dashboard ↗
{01}

Leverage follows liquidity.

The overview describes leverage tiers of 2 to 10× by liquidity class. Open-interest caps are tied to underlying average daily volume and float, with per-position limits. Available leverage is a limit, not a recommended position size.

{02}

No normal fills during a halt.

When the underlying halts, the market blocks normal opens and closes. Any deleveraging follows the published rules. A resumed market must reprice through the gap protocol before regular execution restarts.

{03}

Corporate actions need explicit transitions.

Splits, symbol changes, and delistings are handled by state machines. The specification calls for atomic position scaling across splits and settlement at an attested price for delisted names.

{04}

A defined loss waterfall.

The backend specification orders gap-loss absorption through the insurance fund, then junior insurance capital, then LP principal only in a declared default. This ordering does not guarantee that losses can always be absorbed.

{05}

Risk that remains.

Thin stocks can gap sharply and be difficult to price. Data sources, enclave attestation, software, or market-state handling may fail. Synthetic perpetuals are leveraged exposure and can exhaust all collateral. The dashboard is a preview of these mechanics, not a live trading service.
